title: No bill at the door
note: The bimaristan: endowed, free, teaching hospitals.

research.quotes: heroes.html#f-medicine: 'Al-Razi ran hospitals in Rayy and Baghdad and wrote with a clinical honesty rare in any age.' 'The bimaristan, a Persian word meaning place of the sick, was the Islamic world's hospital, and it ran on a radical rule: no one is turned away.' 'Funded by waqf, a charitable endowment set aside in perpetuity, the great hospitals of Baghdad, Damascus, and Cairo treated rich and poor, resident and stranger, of any faith, without a bill.' 'separate wards for fevers, wounds, and illnesses of the mind, pharmacies on site, physicians on rotation, students trailing their teachers from bed to bed.' 'Cairo's al-Mansuri hospital, opened in 1284, offered music for the sleepless.' 'the ancestor of the teaching hospital and of the conviction that medicine is a public trust.'
research.retell: A doctor named al-Razi worked in early hospitals that treated everyone for free no matter their religion or wealth, and that same idea of a free teaching hospital is still followed by hospitals today.
